source_text:
1.13 Πρὸς ἡμίονον λακτίζουσαν
Οὐδὲν δὲ ὄφελος ὑγιαίνοντος μὲν ὑποζυγίου, στασιάζοντος δὲ ἤτοι ἄλλως
ἀπειθοῦντος ἢ καὶ λακτίζοντος. Εἰς μὲν οὖν τῶν ἵππων τὸ πειθήνιον ἡ Ῥωμαία
πρόκειται φωνή. Λακτίζουσαν δὲ παύσεις ἡμίονον, τὸ τῆς πύξου σπέρμα <καὶ> τοὺς
τριβόλους οἴνῳ ἀφεψήσας καὶ ποτίσας· καί σοι ἐπὶ μῆνας ʹ τιθασὸς μενεῖ.
pass_a_gloss: Toward a kicking mule. No use of a pack-animal healthy but mutinying, either otherwise disobedient or also kicking. Toward the obedience of the horses the Roman voice is-set-forth. A kicking mule you will-stop, having-boiled the seed of box and the caltrops in wine and having-given-it-to-drink; and for you she will-remain tame for [blank-numeral] months.
pass_b_english: For a kicking mule. There is no use in a pack-animal that is healthy but mutinous, either otherwise disobedient or also kicking. For the obedience of horses the Roman voice is set forth. You will stop a kicking mule by boiling the seed of box and the caltrops in wine and giving it to drink; and for you she will remain tame for the months whose numeral is blank in the lock.

choices.term: Εἰς μὲν οὖν τῶν ἵππων τὸ πειθήνιον ἡ Ῥωμαία πρόκειται φωνή
choices.english: For the obedience of horses the Roman voice is set forth
choices.why: The Roman phrase is the 7.6 hoof-charm already given; this chapter does not reprint it, and it is not a spoken order to the mule.

anf_compare.notes: No PD English of the Cesti body; ANF has the letters only.
